venue.name: Canadian Indigenous Art Inc.
venue.description: Canadian Indigenous Art Inc. is a commercial gallery that sells West Coast Indigenous art and runs two shops, one in North Vancouver and one at 78 Wharf St in Nanaimo. It sells wood carvings, masks, paddles, talking sticks, drums, dream catchers, prints, ceramics and jewellery, and says it buys the work directly from the artists at the price they set rather than taking it on consignment. The site is built as an online store with a cart, a checkout and a shipping and returns policy. Nothing on it mentions school visits, daycare visits, group tours, workshops, demonstrations or children's activities, so this is a shop anyone can walk into during opening hours rather than a place that hosts children's groups.
venue.hours_notes: Nanaimo: Monday to Friday 10:00 to 17:30, Saturday 10:00 to 17:00, Sunday 10:00 to 16:00. Their North Vancouver shop keeps different hours.

images.alt: A round wooden panel carved and painted with a stylised face, in red, green, blue and black formline on pale wood with a black rim.

gaps: This is a retail gallery. Every page on the site was searched for the words school, field trip, group visit, tour, workshop, demonstration, children, kids, student, education and class, and none of them appears anywhere, including on the about page, the FAQ page, the contact page, the artists page and both gallery pages. No programme has been recorded, and both the school and daycare fields are set to false on that basis rather than left null.

If you want to take children in, ring the Nanaimo shop on 250-591-4767 first. The site says nothing about whether a group is welcome, how many people fit, whether there is a charge, or whether anything may be touched.
No washrooms, accessibility, stroller access, parking or lunch information is published for either shop.

Their site announced 'The Nanaimo Gallery Has Moved!!' in a notice dated 25 March 2026. The address published everywhere on the site now, including in the FAQ page last updated 28 April 2026 and in the footer of every page, is 78 Wharf St, Nanaimo BC V9R 5G8, so that is what has been recorded. The notice page itself now throws a WordPress error and its text could not be read, so the previous address is not known from the site.

The site publishes no photograph of either shop, inside or out. The only photographs on it are product shots of individual pieces on a plain background, a portrait of the founder on the about page, and a black and white montage of artists holding their work on the FAQ page. The header photo recorded here is therefore a product shot of a carved panel rather than a view of the gallery.

The alt text on that image on the page reads 'Welcome to Canadian Indigenous Art', which is a site slogan rather than a description, so an alt was written here after opening the image in a browser and looking at it.
The og:image on their about page is a broken URL with the protocol and path run together, so it could not be used.
The Nanaimo shop's coordinates are published in the site's own map script on the contact page, as the marker position for the Nanaimo gallery, and were recorded from there.

Prices on the site are for individual pieces of art for sale, not for admission, so no admission figures have been recorded. Their monthly promotion in September 2026 is 10 per cent off Troy Baker and Jacob George plaques until 30 September 2026.

Related record: the catalog already holds mark-loria-gallery-contemporary-indigenous-art.json, a separate Victoria gallery selling contemporary Indigenous art, which is also marked as not serving children's groups.
